statement: A polynomial rolling hash turns a string into a single number, so that two strings can be compared by comparing their numbers. Equal strings always get the same hash; different strings rarely do.

You are given a string text of lowercase letters, an integer base and an integer modulus. Give each letter a value: a = 1, b = 2, …, z = 26. Start with h = 0 and, for each character c of text from left to right, set h = (h × base + value(c)) mod modulus.
This is the same as h = (value(text[0]) × base^(n − 1) + value(text[1]) × base^(n − 2) + … + value(text[n − 1])) mod modulus, where n is the length of text. Return the final h.

examples.explanation: The letter values are 8, 1, 19, 8. The running hash goes 8, 8 × 31 + 1 = 249, 249 × 31 + 19 = 7738, 7738 × 31 + 8 = 239886, which is below the modulus.
Here the running value passes 100003 several times, so it is reduced modulo 100003 after each step; the final hash is 27984.
